Full list: Midvale Water & Sewer Emergency Contacts

Hard floors follow their own rules. Water that slips between luxury vinyl plank or laminate seams gets trapped on the concrete below, so planks may need to be lifted. Hardwood can often be saved with floor drying mats if work starts fast; see Hardwood Floor & Cabinet Drying.

Finished basements in Midvale ramblers and split-levels collect water from window wells, groundwater, water heaters and sewer lines. Paneling over furring strips and carpet over cold concrete hide water well past the visible edge. Basement Flooding Cleanup

Dishwasher lines, fridge ice-maker lines and washer hoses fail without warning, and hard water speeds up wear on valves and fittings. Water runs under cabinets and into the room below. Water Heater & Appliance Leak Cleanup
In stacked buildings, water from one unit travels through ceilings and walls into the next. We extract each affected unit and keep separate records. Condo & Apartment Water Damage
Summer cloudbursts and spring runoff push water down driveways and into window wells, then into basement bedrooms. Window Well Flooding
Businesses along Fort Union Blvd, Union Park Ave, State Street and 7200 South need extraction that limits downtime. Commercial Water Damage
Black water (Category 3): sewer backups, storm runoff and river or canal water. Porous materials are removed, and the area is disinfected and air-scrubbed. See Sewage Backup Cleanup.

When a window well's drain clogs or a downspout empties beside it, water rises above the sill and pours into a basement bedroom. Summer cloudbursts and fast snowmelt cause most of these. Window Well Flooding

Most Midvale water heaters, softeners and washers live in the basement. Hard water wears tanks and valves, and a failed water heater can empty 40 to 50 gallons onto the floor. Frozen pipes in rim joists and outside walls add winter floods. Water Heater & Appliance Leak Cleanup

A blocked or root-filled sewer line pushes waste up through the lowest drain in the house, which is almost always the basement floor drain. This is Category 3 water and needs a different protocol. Sewage Backup Cleanup
Rebuild. Drywall, paneling, carpet, trim and paint go back in. Water Damage Repair

Older homes near Main Street, Center Street and Holden Street often have partial basements, rubble or block foundations, and original clay sewer lines. Floor-drain backups and seepage through older walls are common, and moisture can travel into crawl space sections. Crawl Space Water Damage
Rebuild. Drywall, trim, paint and carpet go back in. Water Damage Repair
If the water also spread to other rooms, see Basement Flooding Cleanup.

We use thermal imaging and moisture meters to trace the water, then dry the cavity directly: baseboards come off, small holes are drilled behind them, and dry air is pushed through the wall. Wet insulation is removed when readings say it can't be dried. Opening a wall a little, in the right place, saves much larger repairs later. Water Leak Detection
Rebuild after the plumber. Once the pipe is repaired, drywall, texture, paint and flooring go back in. Water Damage Repair

That is why quick action and good records matter. Dated photos, moisture readings and a clear record of where the water started help show the damage was sudden. If the pipe served more than one unit, see Condo & Apartment Water Damage.

Offices and shops along Fort Union Blvd, Union Park Ave and State Street often find burst pipes on Monday morning after a cold weekend with the heat turned down. Rentals are similar: a vacant unit between tenants or a basement apartment with the heat off can freeze while nobody is watching. For businesses we schedule drying around opening hours, and for landlords we keep separate records for each unit. Commercial Water Damage
Shut off and drain the swamp cooler line before winter. Swamp Cooler Leak Water Damage
Rebuild. Drywall, flooring and trim go back in. Water Damage Repair
In condos and apartments, a backup in a lower unit can come from waste sent down a shared stack by units above. Condo & Apartment Water Damage

Sewage odor comes from bacteria and from contaminated materials still in the room. Removing those materials is the first step. After that, disinfection, HEPA air scrubbing and drying take care of most odor. For stubborn smells in concrete or framing, sealing and additional odor treatment finish the job. If a musty smell returns weeks later, moisture or mold may be hiding, and the area should be checked. Mold Remediation
Rebuild flooring, drywall and cabinet parts once the plumber has replaced the appliance or line. Water Damage Repair
When water runs under kitchen cabinets or hardwood, see Hardwood Floor & Cabinet Drying.

Newer homes and townhomes around Bingham Junction, Jordan Bluffs and View 72 often put the laundry upstairs. When a washer hose bursts there, water goes through the floor into the ceiling below, down wall cavities and sometimes into the next unit. That means drying two floors at once, checking the ceiling for sagging and, in shared buildings, documenting each unit separately. Condo & Apartment Water Damage
Older homes near Historic Main Street: tanks may sit in partial basements or crawl space areas where leaks go unseen. Crawl Space Water Damage
Businesses on Fort Union Blvd and State Street: water heaters in back rooms and restrooms can flood retail floors overnight. Commercial Water Damage
Hardwood boards cupping at the edges in the kitchen. Hardwood Floor & Cabinet Drying
Water stains on the ceiling under an upstairs laundry or bathroom. Ceiling Water Damage
Moisture meters and thermal imaging can confirm a hidden leak without tearing out cabinets or floors. Water Leak Detection
Repair the ceiling. Damaged drywall is replaced, textured to match, primed and painted. Ceiling Water Damage

Attics are dark, hot in summer and poorly ventilated, which is ideal for mold once wood and insulation get wet. A swamp cooler overflow that goes unnoticed for a week can leave mold on roof sheathing and ceiling joists. If you smell mustiness when the cooler runs or see dark spots around the ceiling vent, have the attic checked. Mold Remediation
Rooftop coolers overflow when a float valve sticks, and central air drain lines clog. Both send water onto the ceiling from above. Swamp Cooler Leak Water Damage
Supply lines running through ceilings, especially near outside walls or over garages, can freeze and split in winter. Burst Pipe Water Damage
In condos, apartments and townhomes, the source is often a washer, dishwasher or water heater in the unit above. Condo & Apartment Water Damage
Replace, texture and paint the ceiling so it blends with the rest of the room. Water Damage Repair

Businesses on Fort Union Blvd, Union Park Ave and 7200 South often have drop ceilings. Wet tiles sag, stain and fall, and water runs along the grid to spread the damage. Wet tiles are replaced, the grid is cleaned, and the space above is dried. Commercial Water Damage
Thermal imaging can confirm whether a ceiling is wet without cutting it open. Water Leak Detection
Crawl spaces get cold in Salt Lake Valley winters, especially near vents and the access hatch. Pipes there freeze and split, and the leak starts when they thaw. Burst Pipe Water Damage
Cracked drain lines under the house can leak sewage directly into the crawl space. Sewage in crawl space cleanup needs full Category 3 handling. Sewage Backup Cleanup
In some older homes, the water heater sits in a crawl space area or a small utility room above it. A failed tank drains straight into the space below. Water Heater & Appliance Leak Cleanup
Dry from below when possible. In homes with a basement or crawl space under the floor, the subfloor is dried from underneath at the same time. Crawl Space Water Damage
Kitchens across Midvale: dishwasher, fridge ice-maker and sink leaks are the most common causes of wet hardwood and cabinets. Water Heater & Appliance Leak Cleanup
The water was sewage or outside floodwater. Sewage Backup Cleanup

Not every wet floor gets wet from above. In homes with a basement or crawl space, a burst pipe, water heater leak or groundwater below can soak the subfloor and push moisture up into the hardwood from underneath. The boards cup even though nothing spilled on top. In these cases, drying has to happen from below as well as above, or the floor will keep cupping. Burst Pipe Water Damage
Through drain stacks: a blockage in a shared stack backs sewage into the lowest unit on that line. Sewage Backup Cleanup
Rebuild each unit once dry. Water Damage Repair
For ceiling damage in the unit below, see Ceiling Water Damage.
For water heater and appliance leaks, see Water Heater & Appliance Leak Cleanup.
Storm runoff at storefront entries and loading docks. Storm Water Damage
Rebuild drywall, flooring, ceiling tiles and finishes. Water Damage Repair

In leased commercial space, responsibility is often split by the lease. The landlord may own the building systems, while the tenant owns improvements and contents. We keep separate records for each, so the landlord, tenant and their insurers each have what they need. Property managers get a single point of contact and a summary across all affected suites. For apartment and condo buildings, see Condo & Apartment Water Damage.

Roof runoff and yard water fill window wells and pour into basement bedrooms. Window Well Flooding
Heavy rain and hail overwhelm gutters and roof drains, sending water through the roof into ceilings. Ceiling Water Damage
Rebuild. Water Damage Repair

Some storm damage is still covered by homeowners policies, such as wind or hail damaging a roof and letting rain inside. Sewer backups caused by a storm usually need a sewer backup endorsement. Sewage Backup Cleanup

Storefronts along State Street, 7200 South and Fort Union Blvd take on water at entry doors and loading docks, and flat commercial roofs back up when roof drains clog. We extract, remove contaminated materials, disinfect and dry with after-hours schedules where possible. Commercial Water Damage

Wood paneling, drywall and carpet over cold concrete trap moisture from leaks, groundwater and humidity. Mold often grows on the back side of paneling and under carpet pad, out of sight. Basement Flooding Cleanup

A slow leak from a supply line, toilet or shower soaks the inside of the wall long before the outside shows it. Black mold behind drywall is often found only when the wall is opened. Water Leak Detection
Swamp cooler overflows, roof leaks, ice dams and bathroom fans venting into the attic all wet the roof deck and insulation. Swamp Cooler Leak Water Damage
Dirt floors, plumbing leaks and groundwater keep crawl spaces damp, especially in older homes near Historic Main Street. Crawl Space Water Damage
Rebuild. Drywall, insulation and finishes go back in. Water Damage Repair

More than half of Midvale homes are rented, and mold in rentals raises extra questions. Tenants often notice the smell or spots first but may not know where the moisture comes from. Landlords need to know whether it's from a leak, a building problem or everyday humidity. Our inspection notes the moisture source and where the growth is, which helps both sides understand what happened. During remediation, containment keeps the work area separate so tenants can usually stay in the rest of the unit. In apartment buildings and condos, we check neighboring units on shared walls and ceilings, because the moisture source is often next door. Condo & Apartment Water Damage
That's why fast drying after any leak is the best mold prevention there is. Emergency Water Extraction
Outside walls: frozen and split pipes near hose bibs and in rim joists. Burst Pipe Water Damage
Basement utility rooms: water heater fittings, softener lines and main valves. Water Heater & Appliance Leak Cleanup
Dry the area. Air movers, dehumidifiers and wall-cavity drying run until readings match the baseline. Emergency Water Extraction
Check for mold where materials stayed wet for a long time. Mold Remediation
Rebuild. Water Damage Repair

In condos and apartments, finding the source decides who is responsible, so accurate mapping across several units matters. For landlords, a moisture map documents a unit at move-in or move-out. For businesses on Fort Union Blvd, Union Park Ave and State Street, quick, low-impact detection means less disruption. Condo & Apartment Water Damage

Matching an existing floor can be tricky, especially older hardwood or discontinued vinyl. Where an exact match isn't available, we talk through options such as replacing a whole room so floors stay consistent. Hardwood Floor & Cabinet Drying
Egress windows and window wells are checked so the room stays safe and dry. Window Well Flooding
This is where rebuild after water damage pays off: getting the basement back as a usable, dry space, not just covering the damage. Basement Flooding Cleanup

Businesses: rebuild is scheduled around opening hours where possible. Commercial Water Damage
If groundwater keeps coming back, we show you which walls took on water so a waterproofing contractor knows where to start. Basement Flooding Cleanup
Water from a split line runs inside walls and ceilings, so thermal imaging and moisture meters guide where to open and dry. Burst Pipe Water Damage

For street flooding, clogged storm drains or water running toward homes during a storm, contact Midvale City Public Works. For flooding that threatens life or involves power lines, call 911. Once your home is safe, storm water inside needs contaminated-water cleanup. Storm Water Damage
Call a water damage crew at (385) 337-3560 to remove the water and dry the structure. Burst Pipe Water Damage

A split pipe inside a wall doesn't just leak onto the floor. Water runs down the inside of the wall cavity, soaks the insulation, pools on the bottom plate and spreads under flooring into the next room. The drywall face may look dry while the inside stays wet. That's why burst pipes need more than a mop and a fan: moisture meters and thermal imaging show how far the water went, and drying has to reach inside the wall cavity. Emergency Water Extraction

More than half of Midvale homes are rented, and many sit in multi-unit buildings. Vacant units between tenants and units with the heat turned down for travel are the most likely to freeze. A burst in one unit can damage the units below and beside it. Landlords and property managers should keep heat on in empty units and check them during cold spells. Tenants should tell their manager right away if water pressure drops during a freeze. Condo & Apartment Water Damage
At that point, the fix usually includes removing wet insulation, drying the attic and ceiling, treating any mold, and replacing ceiling drywall. Swamp Cooler Leak Water Damage

If your home has central air instead of a swamp cooler, ceiling leaks can still happen from a clogged condensate line or drain pan at the indoor coil. Those leaks happen during summer use, not after freezing. If you have a ceiling stain and aren't sure which system caused it, the location usually tells you: under the cooler vent or its duct for a swamp cooler, near the furnace or attic air handler for central air. Ceiling Water Damage

Wet insulation usually has to be removed, the attic dried and new insulation added once everything reads dry. That's why catching a leak early, or preventing it with a proper shutdown, saves so much trouble. Mold Remediation
Start drying. Don't wait for everyone to agree on who pays. Water keeps spreading and the damage grows each day. Condo & Apartment Water Damage
For appliance-related leaks, see Water Heater & Appliance Leak Cleanup.
Finished basements: paneling and drywall over cold concrete in Hillcrest and East Midvale ramblers and split-levels. Basement Flooding Cleanup
If you notice any of these after a leak, the moisture needs to be found and fixed first, then the mold removed properly. Mold Remediation

A leak dried within the first day or two often means extraction, drying and a few small repairs. The same leak left for a week or two can mean opening walls, removing insulation and drywall, containment for mold removal and a much bigger rebuild. General ranges in the Salt Lake area show the difference: drying a room after a leak often runs about $1,000 to $4,500, while mold remediation for small to mid-sized areas often runs about $1,500 to $6,000, before any rebuild. Acting early is the cheapest option by far. Emergency Water Extraction
If you find dampness or spots, stop using the leaking fixture if you can and have the area checked with a moisture meter. Water Leak Detection
Window wells: meltwater and runoff fill the well and pour in around the window. Window Well Flooding

Groundwater seepage is usually wide and shallow. It soaks carpet pad across large areas, wicks up the bottom of drywall and paneling, and gets under laminate and vinyl plank. A shop vac picks up the surface water, but the pad, the bottom of the walls and the floor underneath stay wet. In Midvale's cool basements, that moisture can sit for weeks, which leads to musty smells and mold. Proper drying includes extraction from the pad, moisture mapping of walls and floors, dehumidifiers and air movers, and daily readings until everything matches dry areas. Basement Flooding Cleanup

In heavy runoff years, Salt Lake County and local cities often make sandbags available. Locations change from year to year, so check county and city announcements when high runoff is forecast. Sandbags are most useful at window wells, garage doors and outside basement stairs. They're less useful against groundwater, which comes up from below. Midvale Water & Sewer Emergency Contacts

Seepage water is often clean, but it soaks into carpet pad, the bottom of drywall and paneling, and any cardboard boxes on the floor. Basements stay cool and dark, which slows drying and gives mold a chance to start within a couple of days. A musty smell weeks after the water seemed to stop usually means moisture is still trapped under flooring or inside the walls. Drying it properly the first time is the best way to avoid a mold problem later. Mold Remediation
